Class VanillaScreenPanelRegistry

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.inject.VanillaScreenPanelRegistry
@Internal public final class VanillaScreenPanelRegistry extends Object
Phase 18s — sibling to ScreenPanelRegistry for non-container vanilla screens. Dispatched from ScreenPanelRegistry's AFTER_INIT listener when the opened screen is NOT an AbstractContainerScreen.

Why a sibling registry, not a unified one

Trev's pick on the registry-shape question was "reuse the existing listener, branch on screen type." That settles the EVENT subscription (one listener in ScreenPanelRegistry). The actual dispatch code differs enough (no chrome, no M9 opacity registry, simpler input contract) that bundling it into ScreenPanelRegistry would bloat that already-770-line file. This helper class owns the parallel dispatch path; the existing registry just calls into it.

Lifecycle

  1. Adapter constructor calls trackPending(VanillaScreenPanelAdapter) — adapter joins PENDING, awaiting .on/.onAny targeting declaration.
  2. .on() / .onAny() calls markTargetingDeclared(VanillaScreenPanelAdapter) — adapter moves from PENDING to REGISTERED.
  3. When a matching screen opens, onScreenInit(Screen) matches registered adapters by class-ancestry, registers a Renderable via addRenderableOnly (renders inside Screen.render before the end-of-frame tooltip flush — correct z-order for MK widget tooltips), and registers Fabric input hooks for click/scroll/release dispatch.
  4. unregister() on the adapter calls untrack(VanillaScreenPanelAdapter) — removes from both PENDING and REGISTERED sets. Per-screen Renderables + Fabric hooks auto-clean when the screen closes.

Input contract

On allowMouseClick, returns false (eats the click from vanilla) when any matching adapter's panel is visible and the cursor is within the panel's outer bounds — matches the Panel.opaque(true) default of the container-screen path. Click dispatch is two-pass (active-overlay claim, then hit-test) per the library's existing dispatch discipline.

    • hasOpaqueRegionAt

      public static boolean hasOpaqueRegionAt(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Post-Phase 18r-5: does any registered vanilla-screen adapter's panel claim the cursor point on the given screen — via the unified ScreenPanelRegistry.panelClaimsPoint(Panel, ScreenOrigin, int, double, double) test (opaque background minus holes, active overlay, or solid interactive element)? Used by the widget-hover-suppression mixin so vanilla widgets covered by an MK panel or a dropdown popover stop highlighting on hover.

      Iterates the REGISTERED set (filtered by class-ancestry match against the given screen) rather than a per-screen cached match list — VanillaScreenPanelRegistry doesn't cache matches statically (the dispatch path captures matches in a closure inside onScreenInit(Screen)). Per-call iteration cost is bounded by the total adapter count, which is small for vanilla-screen panels.

    • onScreenInit

      public static void onScreenInit(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Called from ScreenPanelRegistry.onScreenInit(Minecraft, Screen, int, int) when the opened screen is NOT an AbstractContainerScreen. Matches registered adapters against the screen, wires render + input dispatch if any match, no-ops otherwise.
